# keyfile testdata — provenance

> ### These private keys are safe to publish. They are already public.
>
> This directory contains 30 files carrying private key material, in a public
> repository. That is deliberate and safe: **every seed here is a sequential
> byte run printed in an RFC or specification draft** — `0x00..0x1f`,
> `0x00..0x3f`, and one deliberately-corrupted variant. No key generator
> produces those, so none of them can collide with a real key.
>
> **This is enforced, not just asserted.** `testdata_provenance_test.go` fails
> the build if any private key file here has a seed that is not on the published
> list, or if a new private key file appears that nobody listed on purpose. The
> guard has been tested by dropping a randomly-seeded key in and confirming it
> fails — and it reports the failure *without printing the seed*, because a real
> key echoed into CI logs is worse than the file itself.
>
> If that test ever fails for you: do not add your file to the manifest to make
> it pass. Work out first whether it belongs in a public repository at all.

Every fixture here except the two `legacy_*` files was copied from a published
specification, NOT generated by this code. That is the point: a test that passes
against vectors produced by the implementation under test proves only internal
consistency. See `aleutianchain_24` for the same reasoning applied to X-Wing.

## Sources

| Files | Source |
|---|---|
| `mlkem{512,768,1024}_{seed,expanded,both,public}.pem` | RFC 9935 Appendix C (ML-KEM in X.509 / PKCS#8), March 2026 |
| `bad_mlkem512_*.pem` | RFC 9935 Appendix C.4.1 — four deliberately inconsistent keys |
| `mldsa{44,65,87}_{seed,expanded,both,public}.pem` | RFC 9881 Appendix C (ML-DSA in X.509 / PKCS#8), October 2025 |
| `bad_mldsa44_*.pem` | RFC 9881 — deliberately inconsistent keys |
| `xwing_{private,public}.pem` | draft-connolly-cfrg-xwing-kem-10, Appendix D |
| `legacy_xwing_{private,public}.pem` | generated with `github.com/aleutian-ai/xwing-keyfile` v0.2.0, from the same seed as the X-Wing Appendix D example |

The RFC and draft text was fetched directly (`curl`), and the PEM blocks were
extracted programmatically, so no transcription step could alter them. Only line
wrapping was normalised; the base64 content is unchanged, which the
byte-for-byte re-encoding test would catch if it were not.

## The seeds

Both RFCs use the same pattern for their example seeds: 0x00, 0x01, 0x02, …
64 bytes for ML-KEM, 32 for ML-DSA. The X-Wing draft's example uses the same
pattern for its 32-byte seed. The tests assert this, so a fixture swapped for a
different key would fail.

## Bad keys

`bad_*` files are invalid ON PURPOSE. Do not use them for anything but tests.
`keyfile` rejects all of them except `bad_mlkem512_both_1_inconsistent.pem`,
whose expanded half is self-consistent but belongs to another key pair —
detecting that needs an ML-KEM-512 implementation this package does not carry.
That limitation is documented on `CheckConsistency` and asserted in
`TestBadKeysFromTheSpec`.
